contentFull:
Farm visit: BAF Agriculture (part 3) – Chinese integrator Muyuan stepping in

Parts 1 and 2 in this 3-part series introduced Vietnam’s integrator BAF Agriculture and its latest addition, the cutting edge grow-finisher facility Tay An Khanh Farm. It gets even better – this third part explains the role of Chinese integrator Muyuan in the current and future plans.

Vincent ter BeekEditor of Pig Progress / Topic: Pigs around the world

Aug 7

Article

A miniature example of one of the high-rise buildings that will constitute the next building project of BAF Agriculture. Photo: Vincent ter Beek

READ PART 1 AND PART 2

In an attempt to be even better prepared for the future, the Vietnamese integrator BAF Agriculture leaves no stone unturned to make sure each new project is one step ahead of the next one. So Tay An Khanh Farm is more advanced than earlier designs – and the farm that is to follow after this farm will again have additional stories to tell (more about that in the box The next project: high-rise).

As such, Tay An Khanh farm features novelties in comparison to earlier farms, e.g. the farm’s state-of-the-art air filtration system. With pride, Dr Hoang Cong Minh, veterinarian and BAF’s regional southern farm production director, emphasises that the air filtration contains four layers in total. That makes sure that no pathogen whatsoever reaches the pigs inside.

Layer 1 is a fence and is meant to keep out insects and rodents;

Layer 2 – attached straight behind layer 1 – is meant to filter out dust;

Layer 3 is a treatment using water;

Layer 4 is a HEPA filter to keep out viruses like ASF and PRRSv.

Once the air has gone through all the layers, it is being brought into the pig house using numerous red outlets on the side of each pig room. The result is a constant soft air flow, which will keep the temperature for the finishers between 24 and 28°C, depending on outside weather conditions. Air will leave the pig rooms again through the slatted floor, after which de-odorisation is being applied using air scrubbers. That, in itself, however, is not a novelty as earlier BAF farms already applied de-odorisation as well.

A cough monitor which can pick up cough sounds amongst pigs. Photo: Vincent ter Beek

Muyuan Foods

The latest developments were made possible as BAF Agriculture chose to team up with China’s largest pig producer. In the integration’s quest for constant improvement, BAF Agriculture closed a joint venture with Muyuan Foods in September 2025, especially for the construction of this project. In total, BAF Agriculture has 51% of the shares and Muyuan 49% of the shares. That way, the Vietnamese integrator can tap into a large network of experience and technology, the optimised air filtration being one of them.

A spraying device which can spray mist to cool down the pigs in cases of high humidity. Photo: Vincent ter Beek

Hence, an interesting mixture of sensors and electronic gadgets can be spotted in the finisher houses. For some, only one per room is sufficient, others are located in every pen. For instance, on a rail at the ceiling, a heat monitor can scan pen by pen for pigs that might have a higher-than-usual body temperature. Below an additional set of technological novelties is shown.

A temperature monitor as provided by the Chinese integrator Muyuan Foods.

Reflecting on the joint-venture with Muyuan, deputy general director Minh says, “Muyuan and BAF Agriculture have a lot of things in common, as we have the same corporate culture.”. Plus, Muyuan Foods has a strong ambition to grow outside China.” He continues to say, “We aimed to acquire their experience with regard to operational procedures.” So they assisted with consultancy as to the design of the farm. The result is Tay An Khanh farm, the very first of its kind in Vietnam. As far as we are concerned, this cooperation is not a one-off operation. Muyuan Foods is a potential partner for future operations as well.”

A device to monitor and adjust the air flow. Photo: Vincent ter Beek

The next project: high-rise for 64,000 sows

Just like in China, Vietnam will soon also see high-rise pig buildings. After having completed the Tay An Khanh project, the next project will be a farm including eight high-rise pig buildings with six floors, also in the southern cluster, close to Ho Chi Minh City. At the International Pig Veterinary Society congress (June 2026), the company was proudly flaunting a miniature model of the design. Muyuan Foods will once again be closely involved to help coordinate the project.

Each of the eight buildings is intended to house up to 8,400 sows, with the entire complex aimed to house 64,000 sows in total. Each house will produce over 250,000 finishers every year – in official communication BAF Agriculture states to aim for 1.6 million market hogs/year. The complex will include its own feed mill which can provide 600,000 tons of feed. In the immediate surroundings, there will be 2,000 ha space for the cultivation of crops for feed, like cassava, corn as well as bananas.

It is expected that the building of the complex will start in the fourth quarter of 2026 and that the total construction will be ready mid-2028. The idea is that each building will be a farm of its own, with sows, piglets and finisher pigs not having to travel between buildings, only between floors.

Per building there will be around 200 people who will work there during day shifts. Per building there will be dormitories, with employees not being able to visit one another. The total complex will therefore require about 1,600 people.

Deputy general director Nguyen Van Minh is well aware that buildings like those may present their own type of biosecurity risks. He has faith in the expertise of Muyuan Foods as partner in the project, as the Chinese integrator already built many more of these complexes. He says, “Construction comes with higher levels of control and better means than in conventional farms to control the risk.”

Construction costs will amount to 12,000 billion VND (equivalent to €360 million). The company has strong backing from financial institutions and partner banks which are willing to finance the project.

translationZh:
为了在未来做好更充分的准备，越南综合型企业BAF农业不遗余力地确保每个新项目都比上一个项目更领先一步。因此，Tay An Khanh农场比早期的设计更加先进——而紧随其后的下一个农场将会有更多值得讲述的故事（更多内容见框文“下一个项目：高层猪舍”）。

与早期农场相比，Tay An Khanh农场引入了诸多新特色，例如农场最先进的空气过滤系统。BAF农业南部区域生产总监、兽医黄公明博士自豪地强调，空气过滤系统共有四层，确保任何病原体都无法到达猪只身边。

第一层是防护网，用于阻挡昆虫和啮齿动物；

第二层紧接第一层，用于过滤粉尘；

第三层采用水处理；

第四层是HEPA过滤器，用于阻挡非洲猪瘟病毒和猪繁殖与呼吸综合征病毒等病毒。

空气经过所有过滤层后，通过每个猪舍侧面的众多红色出风口被送入猪舍。结果是形成持续柔和的气流，根据外部天气条件，将育肥猪舍的温度保持在24至28摄氏度之间。空气通过漏缝地板排出猪舍，之后使用空气洗涤器进行除臭处理。不过，除臭本身并非新事物，因为BAF早期的农场已经采用了除臭技术。

**牧原食品**

最新进展得益于BAF农业选择与中国最大的生猪生产商合作。在不断追求改进的过程中，BAF农业于2025年9月与牧原食品成立了合资企业，专门用于该项目的建设。BAF农业持有51%的股份，牧原持有49%的股份。这样，越南综合型企业可以借助庞大的经验和技术网络，优化的空气过滤系统就是其中之一。

因此，在育肥舍中可以看到传感器和电子设备的有趣组合。有些设备每个房间只需一个，而另一些则每个猪栏都配备。例如，在天花板的轨道上，一个热监测仪可以逐个猪栏扫描体温可能偏高的猪只。下面展示了更多技术新设备。

牧原食品提供的温度监测仪。

在回顾与牧原的合资合作时，副总经理明表示：“牧原和BAF农业有很多共同点，因为我们有相同的企业文化。”此外，牧原食品在中国以外有强烈的扩张意愿。他继续说道：“我们的目标是获取他们在运营流程方面的经验。”因此，他们在农场设计方面提供了咨询支持。结果就是Tay An Khanh农场，这是越南首个此类农场。就我们而言，这次合作并非一次性操作。牧原食品也是未来运营的潜在合作伙伴。”

用于监测和调节气流的设备。

**下一个项目：可容纳6.4万头母猪的高层猪舍**

就像中国一样，越南很快也将出现高层猪舍建筑。在完成Tay An Khanh项目后，下一个项目将是一个包括八栋六层高层猪舍建筑的农场，同样位于南部集群，靠近胡志明市。在2026年6月的国际猪兽医学会大会上，公司自豪地展示了设计模型。牧原食品将再次密切参与协助协调该项目。

八栋建筑中的每一栋计划容纳多达8400头母猪，整个综合体计划容纳6.4万头母猪。每栋建筑每年将生产超过25万头育肥猪——BAF农业在官方沟通中表示目标是每年160万头市场猪。该综合体将包括自己的饲料厂，可提供60万吨饲料。在周边地区，将有2000公顷土地用于种植饲料作物，如木薯、玉米和香蕉。

预计该综合体将于2026年第四季度开始建设，整个建设将于2028年年中完成。每栋建筑将作为一个独立的农场，母猪、仔猪和育肥猪无需在建筑之间移动，只需在楼层之间移动。

每栋建筑白天班次约有200名员工。每栋建筑都有宿舍，员工之间不能互相拜访。因此，整个综合体总共需要约1600名员工。

副总经理阮文明深知此类建筑可能带来特有的生物安全风险。他对牧原食品作为项目合作伙伴的专业知识充满信心，因为这家中国综合型企业已经建造了许多此类综合体。他说：“与常规农场相比，建设带来了更高水平的控制和更好的风险管理手段。”

建设成本将达到12万亿越南盾（约合3.6亿欧元）。公司得到了金融机构和合作银行的强力支持，这些机构愿意为该项目提供融资。
author: Vincent ter Beek
